title: A private transporter added in DR1 joins the transporter list and can be picked again on the next notification; the frontend keeps it on the one notification it was typed into, so a repeat user retypes the same nine fields every time.

finding.frontend: `/transporters/private` collects the private transporter's name, five address lines, country, telephone number and email address and commits them onto the notification under `privateTransporter` (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/private-transporter-details/private-transporter-details.controller.js). Nothing else reads them. The next notification starts the form blank, and there is nowhere in the service that lists transporters a user has entered before, so a haulier who moves the same animals every week retypes the same record every week.
finding.prototype: Saving on DR1's add-private form pushes the transporter onto the user's own transporter records, and the `/transporter` list is built by concatenating those with the eight the service ships (app/routes.js:2903-2905, 3310-3345). The record the user just added is on the list the moment they return to it, alongside the approved ones, with its own Type and Status. Where the add was started from the address book, the same save also copies it into the address book.
finding.difference: Give a transporter somewhere to live other than the notification. That is a persistence change first — a per-organisation transporter collection, or an extension of the address book to carry a transporter's approval number, which the frontend's own note says the address book cannot represent today. Once records survive a notification, the list page shows them and the private form becomes an add-to-the-list step rather than a fill-in-the-blanks step. Ordered after the list page exists; useless before it.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding the frontend writing the private transporter anywhere other than the notification's own answers — an address-book write, a per-organisation collection, or any read of previously entered transporters when the form loads.
finding.correction: CLAIMED: DR1 keeps an added private transporter on a reusable list, the frontend keeps it on the one notification, and persistence has to change first. VERIFIED ON BOTH SIDES. DR1 unshifts the new record onto sessionData.addedTransporters and builds the list page by concatenating those with the eight it ships (app/routes.js:3310-3316, 2903-2905), and copies it into the address book when the add was started from there. The frontend commits the fields onto the notification's own answers and nothing else reads them. BAND CONFIRMED FROM A REAL DEPENDENCY: the frontend has no per-organisation collection to write to and the notification is the only thing that persists, so a transporter register or an address-book extension has to exist before reuse means anything — the frontend's own commercial-transporter module records why the address book cannot stand in. MIS-CITED, slot left as it stands: evidence.frontend points at src/server/app/services/commercial-transporters/records.js:1-6, which is that comment rather than the private form this finding is about; the primary frontend citation should be src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/private-transporter-details/private-transporter-details.controller.js. ONE THING TO KNOW BEFORE BUILDING: DR1's reuse is prototype session storage, not a database. It survives the notification but not the session, so DR1 shows the intent rather than the mechanism, and the shape of the store is the frontend's to decide. CONTROL FIXED: this finding named `privateTransporter`, which is the key the answers are committed under and not a thing anyone can point at on a page — no element on fe-transporter-private carries that name, so it resolved to nothing and no crop was taken. The page's own first field is `nameOrOrganisationName`, and that is what is named now; the nine boxes this finding says a repeat user retypes are `nameOrOrganisationName`, `addressLine1`, `addressLine2`, `townOrCity`, `county`, `postalOrZipCode`, `country`, `telephoneNumber` and `emailAddress`, and a crop of the first of them frames the form the finding is about. The frontend slot still says `privateTransporter` and should, because that is the correct name for where the answers land.

relatedTo.why: Reuse has no surface until the list page exists
